conviction_note: Small positive lean: the $0.57 bar sits below Q2's $0.59 while management guided Q3 NIM back toward Q1's 3.15% and retired $40m of 6.98% sub-debt on Jul 1, credit was improving and the stock trades below tangible book with an active buyback; offset by the Sept 16 Fed hike landing on a self-described liability-sensitive balance sheet, which threatens the Q4 margin commentary on the Oct 20 call. abs_move 3.0 (mean abs of 7 prints 2.75, median 1.85, no option chain, two of the last four prints moved 5-7%), p_up 57 → +0.42; findings sum +0.6, the two agree in sign.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus EPS $0.57, revenue ~$34.07M; two agreeing sources: Earnings Whispers https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/RBB and a Zacks preview (EPS $0.57, -3.4% y/y, revenue $34.07M, revised -0.34% over 30 days) surfaced via search on zacks.com. No numeric company EPS guide; company guided qualitatively (NIM back to around Q1 level, expenses at high end of $18-19M, tax ~28%) on the Jul 21 call https://www.earningswhispers.com/transcript/RBB/Q22026

findings.finding: The $0.57 consensus is below Q2's reported $0.59 even though management on the Jul 21 call guided Q3 NIM back to 'just around where we were able to achieve in the first quarter' (3.15%, vs Q2 3.06%), expected second-half loan growth of mid-single digits annualised, and on Jul 1 redeemed $40m of the sub-notes that had repriced to 6.98% (the remaining $80m reset to 7.02%); a 9bp NIM recovery on ~$3.9B of earning assets is roughly $0.9m a quarter pre-tax, about $0.04 a share at the 28% tax rate, so the guide-implied pre-provision path is ~$0.62-0.64 and the $0.57 bar embeds a provision or expense drag that Q2 (zero provision, $0.22m OREO loss) did not have.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 EPS $0.59 vs $0.41 consensus: +6.76%; Q1 2026 $0.66: +5.45%; Q2 2026 $0.59 vs $0.53-0.54 (an 11% beat): -0.41%. Beats have been bought two times of three; the last one was not.
findings.why_not_priced: If the street had carried the NIM guide and sub-debt saving through, consensus would sit at or above Q2's $0.59 rather than $0.57 (-3.4% y/y, revised slightly lower in the last 30 days), and the stock would not be at ~0.94x tangible book ($25.6 vs TBV $27.23 at June 30) after a -4.3% 20-day drift.
findings.independence: Call transcript with the NIM and loan-growth guide is a separate document: https://www.earningswhispers.com/transcript/RBB/Q22026 (2026-07-21). Both are company sources; the arithmetic is mine.

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 (12-0); RBB described itself on the Jul 21 call as liability sensitive, carries ~$1.5B of CDs maturing within 12 months at ~3.60% (40% repricing in Q3 at ~3.70%), Flex Savings in the 'high threes', and $80m of floating sub-debt already at 7.02% that resets quarterly, so the Q4 margin outlook given on the Oct 20 call is more likely to be flat or down than the 'improving' path guided in July.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 NIM fell 9bp on the sub-debt repricing and the stock moved -0.41% despite an 11% EPS beat, the only beat in the history that was not bought.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is -4.3% over 20 days and sits below tangible book, which is what a market discounting margin pressure would look like. The hike came after the company last spoke, so the forward NIM commentary has not been updated; the Q3 print itself carries only two weeks of it.
findings.independence: Company liability-sensitivity statement and CD maturity schedule from the Q2 call: https://www.earningswhispers.com/transcript/RBB/Q22026. Macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by the company since the hike; proxy.

findings.finding: Credit was improving into Q3: nonperforming loans fell 47% to $23.8m (0.72% of loans), special mention fell to $20.3m from $24.8m, NCOs 0.01%, ACL 1.32% covering NPLs 184%, and the largest problem credit, a $19.4m partially completed construction project, moved to OREO with an as-is appraisal supporting carrying value and management 'looking for a resolution in the second half'; a sale or continued zero provision would beat a bar that appears to embed a provision.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026, which carried a $0.89m OREO gain and a provision reversal, moved +5.45%; Q2 2026 with a $0.22m OREO loss and zero provision moved -0.41%.
findings.why_not_priced: A bar at $0.57 below Q2's $0.59 with revenue guided up is consistent with the street carrying a provision of roughly $1-2m; if it expected continued benign credit the bar would be higher. The OREO sale is binary (a write-down is the left tail), which is why the range is wide.
findings.independence: Same Q2 release as finding 1 for the credit metrics (shared document, different line); OREO resolution timing from the call transcript https://www.earningswhispers.com/transcript/RBB/Q22026.

findings.finding: Capital return below book: RBB bought ~181,000 shares in Q2 at ~$24.65-24.75, authorised a new 1m-share (~6%) plan through June 2028, and shares outstanding fell further from 16,985,919 (Jun 30) to 16,915,964 (Jul 31, 10-Q cover) with the stock trading below tangible book ($27.23); the CFO said a dividend increase is 'something we would consider'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 release announced the new buyback plan and the stock moved -0.41%; no prior dividend-raise reaction in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: The July share count is in a 10-Q cover page nobody aggregates; a dividend increase from $0.16 would be news on the release. If priced, the stock would not sit at ~0.94x TBV.
findings.independence: Buyback size and dividend comment from the call transcript https://www.earningswhispers.com/transcript/RBB/Q22026; plan and shares from the Q2 release (shared with findings 1 and 3).

findings.finding: The bank's Chief Operations Officer Gary Fan leaves on 2026-09-30 under a non-renewal agreed Aug 31, tied to the leadership transition plan, with six months of base salary as severance; a small Q3/Q4 expense item and continued executive turnover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved print in the baseline turned on an executive change; the 2024-25 CEO transition preceded the window.
findings.why_not_priced: Public 8-K, so the fact is priced; only the expense recognition in the quarter is not visible. Sized as a one-off fraction.

findings.finding: Peer read from banks that reported after RBB last spoke is mixed on funding: Regions (Oct 16) NIM +2bp to 3.68% with deposit costs held, Independent Bank Corp deposit costs +6bp q/q offset by asset repricing; for a CD-heavy, liability-sensitive bank the deposit-cost half is the more relevant read.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No company-specific history on peer read-throughs.
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy only; peers are much larger, asset-neutral or asset-sensitive, and not in RBB's Chinese-American CRE niche. Direct peers (Cathay, Hanmi, Preferred, Hope, East West) had not reported by 2026-10-19.
findings.independence: Independent Bank Corp Q3 release: https://finviz.com/news/403305/independent-bank-corp-reports-third-quarter-net-income-of-897-million. Proxy.

baseline_tension: No skew to agree or disagree with; the mild positive lean cuts against the -4.3% 20-day drift, but that drift is plausibly the September hike on a liability-sensitive bank, which is why finding 2 offsets part of finding 1 and p_up stays at 57.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6/core table (inside what the company guided): the NIM-recovery finding lands largely inside management's July guide, trimmed +0.8 -> +0.6.
Lesson 5 (macro-to-company proxy): the Fed-hike guidance finding trimmed -0.5 -> -0.4 and the peer read -0.2 -> -0.1, both filed, not dropped.
Lesson 1 (verified fact vs reaction): last beat (Q2, +11%) was sold to -0.41%, which keeps p_up at 57 rather than higher; two earlier beats were bought, so not cut further.
Lesson 7: short interest looked up before the negatives (3.1%, 4.68 DTC, falling) — not crowded, negatives not shrunk for squeeze risk.
Lesson 8: thin coverage keeps abs_move at 3.0 above the 1.85 median.
